title: Question-focused forms
summary: Break complex data collection into understandable questions or sections, asking only for information needed for the user's goal.
problem: Large undifferentiated forms increase scanning effort, error rates, and uncertainty about why information is required.
use_when: A transaction asks for multiple concepts or conditional information
Users benefit from a clear sense of one decision at a time
avoid_when: The form is genuinely short and can be understood as one compact unit
Splitting would force unnecessary navigation for tightly related fields
rationale: Focused questions reduce simultaneous cognitive load.
Conditional questions can avoid collecting irrelevant data.

prefer_alternatives_if: The entire form is only a few tightly related fields
use_if: A transaction asks for multiple concepts or conditional information
Users benefit from a clear sense of one decision at a time

requirements: Group related controls with semantic fieldsets/legends where applicable.
Maintain a logical heading and focus order.
Do not rely on visual grouping alone.
Explain why sensitive or unexpected information is required.
Keep progress understandable for longer flows.
